newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast spot prods prices lifted by NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast spot prods prices lifted by NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices got a lift Thursday from futures markets, with diesel fuels rising one cent amid talk that a trading house looked to export diesel fuel to Asia, traders said.
June NYMEX heating oil rose 1.30 cents a barrel on the backs of rallies in unleaded gasoline and crude futures.
++ Diesel. May low sulphur diesel fuel rose 1.50 cents a gallon Thursday to 54.50/55.50 cents, with talk that Astra Oil Company Inc would load up two 300,000 barrel ships.
Astra declined comment except to say there were opportunities to make money elsewhere with California prices low.
"The window is open for it to leave," a broker said.
++ Gasoline. Conventional grade unleaded gasoline rose one cent a gallon from Wednesday to 60/61 cents in Los Angeles, with San Francisco grades talked 1.25 cents lower.
Prompt CARB gasoline ranged 63/64 cents a gallon, with June shipments valued one cent higher.
"Gas is up in June...traders are thinking demand will be up," one traders said.
Bids for CARB unleaded gasoline also gained one cent, with traders pegging offers at 64 cent and bids at 63 cents.
